The mean of n terms is x¯. If the first term is increased by 1 , second by 2 and so on, then the new mean is:
questions.explanation:
We have,

Mean of n terms is x¯

Therefore, x¯=x1+x2+x3+……+xnn ...(i)

Since, it is given that the first term is increased by 1, second by 2 and so on.

That means, the n terms become

x1+1,x2+2,x3+3,……,xn+n.

So, the new mean X¯ is,

⇒X¯=x1+1+x2+2+x3+3+…..+xn+nn⇒X¯=x1+x2+x3+…..+xn+(1+2+3+…+n)n

From eq (i),

⇒X¯=x¯+(1+2+3+…+n)n⇒X¯=x¯+n(n+1)2n⇒X¯=x¯+(n+1)2

The mean of the data set comprising of 16 observations is 16. If one of the observation valued 16 is deleted and three new observations valued 3,4 and 5 are added to the data, then the mean of the resultant data, is
questions.explanation:
We’re given:

Original number of observations: 16

Original mean: 16

So, the total sum of the original data is:

Total Sum=16×16=256\text{Total Sum} = 16 \times 16 = 256

Now:

One observation valued 16 is deleted → new sum: 256−16=240256 - 16 = 240

Three new observations added: 3, 4, 5 → added sum: 3+4+5=123 + 4 + 5 = 12

New total sum: 240+12=252240 + 12 = 252

New number of observations: 16−1+3=1816 - 1 + 3 = 18

Now calculate the new mean:

New Mean=25218=14\text{New Mean} = \frac{252}{18} = 14
